cues.en: of conversations with Tyler.

cues.en: research to bear on the most pressing issues facing our country today.

cues.en: This series of conversations will bring together world-class leaders who will talk about how

cues.en: blog Marginal Revolution.

cues.en: He is also cofounder of Marginal Revolution University, an innovative space for learning

cues.en: and teaching economics online.

cues.en: Bloomberg called Tyler “America’s hottest economist.”

cues.en: Foreign Policy has named him to the Global Top 100 Thinkers.

cues.en: For those of us who have had an opportunity to have a conversation with Tyler, we know

cues.en: that his mind is an ever-changing kaleidoscope.

cues.en: We can discuss the NBA, arts, music, literature, even economics, and sometimes public policy.

cues.en: I’m really pleased to share him with you today.

cues.en: public intellectuals of our entire time.

cues.en: Throughout the course of history, he will be recognized as such.

cues.zh: 我觉得 Peter 绝对是开启这个系列的最佳人选。
cues.en: I thought Peter would be absolutely the perfect person to inaugurate this series.

cues.en: Peter himself doesn’t need an introduction; he has a best-selling book.

cues.en: His role in PayPal, Facebook, Palantir, many other companies, is well known.

cues.en: Peter is a dynamo.

cues.zh: 没有人像 Peter 那样。
cues.en: There is no one like Peter.

cues.zh: 但今天的目的是聚焦 Peter 作为公共知识分子的观点。
cues.en: But the purpose today is to focus on Peter’s views as a public intellectual.

cues.en: The way we run these dialogues are a bit different than usual.

cues.zh: 不会闲聊拖沓。
cues.en: It’s not going to be chatty and drawn out.

cues.zh: 我们会尝试重现 Peter 和我彼此之间那种对话。
cues.en: We’ll try to replicate a kind of conversation Peter and I would have with each other.

cues.zh: 直奔主题，大量快速来回，我们看看在公开场合能做得
cues.en: Get right to the point, a lot of quick back and forth, and we’ll see how well we can

cues.en: do that in public.

cues.en: But I’ve watched a lot of interviews with Peter online and we’re going to try to make

cues.en: this different from all those.

cues.zh: Peter，我们从一些关于停滞的问题开始吧。
cues.en: Let’s start with some questions about stagnation, Peter.

cues.zh: 任何时候，如果你想补充自己的其他话题，请尽管说。
cues.en: At any point, if you care to add other topics of your own, please do so.

cues.zh: 你因主张——嗯——“他们承诺给我们飞车，而我们只得到
cues.en: You’re well known for arguing, well, “they promised us flying cars and all we got is

cues.zh: 140 个字符”；“技术进步已经放缓了。”
cues.en: 140 characters”; “technological progress has slowed down.”

cues.zh: 你认为，当那种情况
cues.en: How is it you think that we’re most likely to get out of the great stagnation, when that

cues.zh: 发生时，我们最有可能如何走出大停滞？
cues.en: happens?

cues.zh: PETER THIEL：是的，我认为存在——那三件彼此独立的事。
cues.en: PETER THIEL: Yes, I think there are, those three separate things.

cues.zh: 问题在于停滞，而我认为，这种停滞一直发生在
cues.en: There’s the question of stagnation, which I think has been a story of stagnation in

cues.zh: 原子世界，而非比特世界。
cues.en: the world of atoms, not bits.

cues.zh: 我认为，在计算机、信息技术、互联网、
cues.en: I think we’ve had a lot of innovation in computers, information technology, Internet,

cues.zh: 移动互联网这些比特世界的领域，我们有很多创新。
cues.en: mobile Internet in the world of bits.

cues.zh: 在原子世界就没那么多：超音速旅行、太空旅行、新能源、
cues.en: Not so much in the world of atoms, supersonic travel, space travel, new forms of energy,

cues.zh: 新的药物形式、新的医疗设备等等。
cues.en: new forms of medicine, new medical devices, etc.

cues.zh: 这算是创新的一个双轨领域。
cues.en: It’s sort of been this two-track area of innovation.

cues.zh: 关于它因何而起有很多疑问，我觉得这也许是个不错的切入点
cues.en: There are a lot of questions of what has caused it and I think maybe that’s a good part

cues.zh: 来开始讨论怎么摆脱它。
cues.en: to start in terms of what gets you out of it.

cues.zh: 初步来看，我会说我们生活在一个比特不受监管
cues.en: On a first cut, I would say that we lived in a world in which bits were unregulated

cues.zh: 而原子受监管的世界里。
cues.en: and atoms were regulated.

cues.zh: 如果你创办一家计算机软件公司，大概花10万美元；而要让一种新药
cues.en: If you are starting a computer software company, that costs maybe $100,000, to get a new drug

cues.zh: 通过FDA，可能得花10亿美元左右。
cues.en: through the FDA, maybe on the order of a billion dollars or so.

cues.zh: 如果FDA监管电子游戏技术，而你不得不做双盲研究来
cues.en: If the FDA were regulating video game technologies, and you had to do a double-blind study to

cues.zh: 确保电子游戏不会让人上瘾、损害大脑等等。
cues.en: make sure that the video games weren’t addictive, damaging to your brain, etc.

cues.zh: 这些事情都是被多重因素过度决定的。
cues.en: These things are very overdetermined.

cues.zh: 它由许多不同因素驱动。
cues.en: It’s driven by many different factors.

cues.zh: 我试图摆脱它的狭隘尝试，并不一定是来华盛顿
cues.en: My narrow attempt to get out of it is not necessarily to come to DC and beg the regulators

cues.zh: 恳求监管者更讲道理。
cues.en: to be more reasonable.

cues.zh: 这只是想设法帮人们在边缘领域取得成功。
cues.en: It is just to try to find ways for people to succeed at the margins.

cues.zh: 因为我认为，导致停滞的另一个因素是滞后效应。
cues.en: Because I think the other thing that has driven the stagnation is the hysteresis.

cues.zh: 当你有一段失败史，这会让人气馁，于是失败招致更多失败。
cues.en: When you have a history of failure, that becomes discouraging and so failure begets failure.

cues.zh: 如今，但凡头脑正常的父母都不会鼓励孩子去学核工程，而
cues.en: No halfway sane parent would encourage their kids to study nuclear engineering today, whereas

cues.zh: meanwhile 有很多人投身软件行业。
cues.en: there are a lot of people going into software.

cues.zh: 软件领域的成功历史正鼓励更多人进入这一行，推动更多创新。
cues.en: The history of success in software is encouraging more people to go into it and drive more innovation.

cues.zh: 而其他这些领域的失败历史则一直非常令人泄气。
cues.en: Then the history of failure in these other areas has been very discouraging.

cues.zh: 我认为，如果你能在其他领域取得一些标志性的成功，那就能
cues.en: What I think would start, if you got some signal successes in other areas, that can

cues.zh: 树立先例，从而设法把原本的恶性循环变成良性
cues.en: then set a precedent and you can somehow get what’s been a vicious cycle into a virtuous

cues.zh: 循环。
cues.en: cycle.

cues.zh: TYLER COWEN: 那么如果你必须做个预测，具体哪项突破会
cues.en: TYLER COWEN: Then if you have to make a prediction, which breakthrough in particular will get

cues.zh: 让我们走出停滞？
cues.en: us out of the stagnation?

cues.zh: 你会选哪个？
cues.en: What’s your pick?

cues.zh: PETER THIEL: 我仍认为——最自然的候选大概都是那些
cues.en: PETER THIEL: I still think there are—probably the most natural ones are all these things

cues.zh: 处在信息技术与原子边界上的东西，是比特与原子。
cues.en: that are at the boundary of information technology on atoms, of bits and atoms.

cues.zh: TYLER COWEN: 人工智能？
cues.en: TYLER COWEN: Artificial intelligence?

cues.zh: 生物科技？
cues.en: Biotech?

cues.zh: PETER THIEL: AI 感觉有点被过度炒作了。
cues.en: PETER THIEL: AI feels slightly overhyped.

cues.zh: 生物科技，可能会有很多进展。
cues.en: Biotech, a lot could happen.

cues.zh: 但它感觉受到严格监管。
cues.en: It feels heavily regulated.

cues.zh: 但如果有自动驾驶汽车，那会是一项重大创新，会
cues.en: But if you’ve got self-driving cars, that would be a significant innovation which would

cues.zh: 在边际上带来不小的改变。
cues.en: change a decent amount at the margins.

cues.zh: 它面临一些监管挑战，但它差不多正处在
cues.en: There’s some regulatory challenges with it, but it’s sort of right at the intersection

cues.zh: 各种可能发生的事情的交汇点。
cues.en: of the kinds of things that could happen.

cues.zh: 我认为最自然的希望是，信息技术开始扩展，并开始
cues.en: I think the most natural hope is that information technology starts to broaden out and starts

cues.zh: 影响这个由原子构成的世界。
cues.en: to impact this world of atoms.

cues.zh: 接下来我们会面对这个问题：技术是否跑得比政治快
cues.en: Then we’re going to have this question about whether the technology outpaces the politics

cues.zh: 还是反过来。
cues.en: or vice versa.

cues.zh: TYLER COWEN：我该盯着哪个数字？
cues.en: TYLER COWEN: What number should I keep my eye on?

cues.zh: 假设你要去睡个长觉，我需要有人告诉我：“Tyler，
cues.en: Let’s say you’re going to take a long nap and I need someone to tell me, “Tyler,

cues.zh: 我们现已走出大停滞了。”
cues.en: we’re out of the great stagnation now.”

cues.zh: 我该看哪个客观指标？
cues.en: What’s the impersonal indicator that I should look at?

cues.zh: PETER THIEL：我不同意这个问题的前提。
cues.en: PETER THIEL: I disagree with the premise of that question.

cues.zh: 我不认为未来是某种固定存在的东西。
cues.en: I don’t think the future is this fixed thing that just exists.

cues.zh: 我不认为大停滞的结束与否是自动发生的。
cues.en: I don’t think there’s something automatic about the great stagnation ending or not ending.

cues.zh: 我认为——我一直相信人的能动性，所以我认为这很大程度上取决于
cues.en: I think—I always believe in human agency and so I think it matters a great deal whether

cues.zh: 人们是否终结它。
cues.en: people end it or not.

cues.zh: Kurzweil 有本极度乐观的书《The Singularity Is Near》；我们当时有
cues.en: There was this sort of hyperoptimistic book by Kurzweil, The Singularity Is Near; we had

cues.zh: 各种加速上升的图表。
cues.en: all these sort of accelerating charts.

cues.zh: 我也不同意这一点，不仅是因为我更悲观，而且我也不认同
cues.en: I also disagree with that, not just because I’m more pessimistic, but I disagree with

cues.zh: 这样一种未来设想：你只需舒舒服服地坐着、吃着爆米花，看着
cues.en: the vision of the future where all you have to do is sit back, eat popcorn, and watch

cues.zh: 未来的大戏自然上演。
cues.en: the movie of the future unfold.

cues.zh: 我认为未来掌握在我们手中，取决于我们选择做什么。
cues.en: I think the future is open to us to decide what to do.

cues.zh: 如果你选择躺平，如果你鼓励所有人也都去躺平，那么大停滞
cues.en: If you take a nap, if you encourage everybody else to take a nap, then the great stagnation

cues.zh: 就永远不会结束。
cues.en: is never going to end.

cues.zh: 已经彻底改变了？
cues.en: have so changed?

cues.en: Some writers have suggested the decline of mainline Protestantism has intellectually

cues.zh: 永远改变了美国。
cues.en: changed America forever.

cues.zh: 人们对“能成就什么”的认知变了，我们不再愿意去重复，比如曼哈顿
cues.en: The sense of what can be accomplished, our unwillingness to repeat, say, the Manhattan

cues.zh: 工程，或是阿波罗计划。
cues.en: Project, or Apollo.

cues.zh: 有没有可能我们就是永远陷入了这种境地，陷入恶性循环，陷得越久，
cues.en: Is it possible we’re simply in that forever, and it’s a downward spiral and the longer

cues.zh: 就越难挣脱出来？
cues.en: you’re in it, the harder it is to get out?

cues.zh: 这其实并不关乎比特。
cues.en: It’s not really about bits.

cues.zh: 彼得·蒂尔：确实有可能是那样。
cues.en: PETER THIEL: It’s certainly possible that it’s something like that.

cues.zh: 但我确实认为，在边际上，总还是有些事情
cues.en: But I do think that there’s certainly, at the margins, there always are things that

cues.zh: 是我们能做的。
cues.en: we can do.

cues.zh: 对于政府能否成为扭转
cues.en: I am somewhat pessimistic about the possibility of government being a key, a place where the

cues.zh: “大停滞”的关键，我持相当悲观的态度。
cues.en: great stagnation gets reversed.

cues.en: There is a sense in which a letter from Einstein to the White House would get lost in the mail

cues.zh: 恐怕在收发室就会被弄丢。
cues.en: room today.

cues.zh: 今天甚至连阿波罗计划都搞不成了。
cues.en: You could not even do Apollo.

cues.en: Even something like the SDI program in the 1980s.

cues.en: The debate in the ’80s was, it’s a dangerous first-strike weapon versus a great defensive

cues.en: technology, whereas today, people would say that SDI was just this fictional thing that

cues.zh: 根本就不可能成功。
cues.en: would have never worked.

cues.zh: 说真的，我们预期大幅降低的方式，实在是匪夷所思。
cues.en: Again, this very odd way that our expectations have been dramatically reduced.

cues.zh: 但我确实认为这存在一个问题：私营部门究竟能在何处
cues.en: But I do think there’s sort of a question about where in the private sector can you

cues.zh: 实现足够大尺度的协作。
cues.en: coordinate things on a big enough scale.

cues.zh: 硅谷初创公司曾是一种实现方式，也许还有某一类
cues.en: Silicon Valley start-ups have been a way to do it, and maybe there’s some class of somewhat

cues.zh: 规模稍大一些的企业。
cues.en: larger companies.

cues.en: My PayPal colleague Elon Musk started both SpaceX and Tesla, which are extremely charismatic

cues.en: businesses, because it involved somewhat larger-scale complex coordination, getting a lot of different

cues.zh: 环节整合到一起运转。
cues.en: pieces together to work.

cues.zh: 这或许比不上一个高效运转的政府所能达到的规模。
cues.en: Not as big as we could do, perhaps, if you had a well-functioning government.

cues.zh: 但我认为那其实不太现实。
cues.en: But I think that’s not really that realistic.

cues.en: I would say, they are still higher than they were in 2002, 2003 on the oil side.

cues.en: The jury is still very much out on how well it’s going to work.

cues.en: I think the big question is, what’s the equilibrium price at which fracking is really

cues.en: going to work?
